input.brief: Cyber Y2K streetwear edit: chrome puffers, mesh tops, platform boots picked from AliExpress, SHEIN and Bulchic; every piece has an item ID from Instagram

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Inset photograph, crossing wordmark
hero.blueprint: One deep, dark flat field. A tall portrait photograph fills the left 47% of the viewport, inset 20px from the top, left and bottom edges, with a 12px radius and object-fit: cover; it is position: sticky for the length of the page while the right side scrolls. Five text links at 15px sit top-right on a 32px margin, the last of them the single action. There is no logo at the top. In the right half, at 44% of the height and centred on that half's own axis, one supporting sentence in the light ink at 24px on up to three lines, max 26ch. Along the bottom runs the name in lowercase at clamp(120px, 12vw, 200px), light or regular weight, tracking -0.04em, on one line. It starts over the photograph's lower-right corner, overlapping the image by about 10% of the viewport width (z-index above it; mix-blend-mode: difference keeps the letters legible on the picture), and ends flush with the right margin, its baseline 40px above the bottom edge.
hero.mobile: The photograph takes the top 58% of the screen, inset 12px, with the same radius. The name runs under it at 21vw on one line, its ascenders overlapping the photograph's bottom edge by 3vw. The sentence follows at 17px, left-aligned on a 20px margin. Links reduce to a menu word and the action on the top row, set over the photograph.
hero.headline: The name in lowercase on one line, up to 9 characters at this size; a longer name drops to 9vw.

type.note: A tall American gothic taken from city signage, blunt and civic, over a plain public-service sans. Suits culture indexes, community projects, bars, sport clubs and local campaigns.

palette.name: Cool grey, cobalt
palette.note: Cool pale grey holds the page with near-black type and nothing else tinted. Cobalt starts as the button and one highlighted sentence, takes one whole section as a flat field with white text, then returns as a single button block.

motion.name: Scaling wordmark
motion.description: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy. Travel stays under 8%. Static fallback where scroll timelines are unsupported. Recipe: 'Scroll-linked progress' in references/motion.md, animating `scale`.

sections.name: Square plate, spare text
sections.blueprint: One flat field split 50/50, at least 88svh tall. Left half: a single square photograph filling the half's width minus 40px margins, vertically centred, square corners. A large simple shape may be laid over it to turn the photograph into the object it stands for: a ring 86% of its width with a 6px stroke and a small solid dot at the centre makes a record; a notch cut by clip-path makes a ticket stub. Right half, a flex column with space-between: at the top a row of three plain text tabs at 18px (editions, years, variants), the active one in full ink and the others at 40%; in the middle the title, two to four words at 32–40px bold, with a 34ch description 48px below; along the bottom two filled rectangular cells side by side, each half the column wide and 72px tall, acting as the two actions, one in ink and one a tone off the field.
sections.mobile: The square photograph comes first at full width with 16px margins. The tabs sit under it as one row at 17px. Then the title at 28px, the description, and the two action cells stacked, each full width and 60px tall.

sections.name: One item per poster line
sections.blueprint: A short list set as a poster. Four to seven items (services, headline acts, courses, opening days) stack one per line at clamp(64px, 10vw, 150px) in the display weight, all capitals or all lowercase, leading 0.92, flush left at a 20px margin on a flat field. Its one detail (a price, a date, a time range) sits at the right margin on the same baseline at 18–20px with tabular figures, so the page has two alignments only: giant words left, small facts right. Items too long for one line at this size are shortened, not shrunk. Between items there is only the tight leading. Hovering an item swaps its ink for the accent. There is no heading: the first item starts 80px below the section top and the last ends 80px above the bottom. The list reuses the hero title's exact type size, so it reads as another poster.
sections.mobile: Items at 15vw, one per line, flush left with 16px margins. Each detail moves beneath its item at 15px, left-aligned, with 6px above and 22px below. If any single word is wider than the screen at 15vw, drop the whole list to 12vw rather than breaking a word.

sections.name: Staggered pairs in empty ground
sections.blueprint: No heading. Photographs are placed one or two per screen so that more than half of every screen stays empty ground. Screen one: a 3:4 portrait in columns 1–4 against the left margin, and a near-square 5:4 image in columns 7–12 against the right margin whose top edge starts 30vh lower than the portrait's. Screen two: a 3:2 landscape in columns 6–11 and, 24vh lower, a small 4:5 image in columns 2–4. Repeat the two arrangements, mirrored on the second pass, for six to ten photographs. Under each image's left corner, a one-line caption at 13px in the soft ink, 10px below the image. Vertical gaps between pairs are 22–28vh. Every edge sits on a column line and offsets come from only two values. Square corners. If motion is used, images enter with a short `clip-path` wipe from the bottom edge.
sections.mobile: A single column in which widths and sides alternate: 70% against the left margin, 84% against the right, 56% left, then 100% full-bleed, with 64px between images. Captions sit under each image's left corner at 13px. Portrait crops are preferred so each image fills most of the screen height.

sections.name: One verb at a time
sections.blueprint: Three to five full-bleed panels, each 100svh tall, stacked with no gap; each is one stage and holds one photograph covering it. In every panel a single word, the verb for that stage ('Cut', 'Fold', 'Stitch', 'Press'), is set at clamp(96px, 17vw, 300px), heavy and centred, inside a wrapper that is position: sticky; top: 50% and shifted up by half its own height. Because each word is sticky only within its own panel, it holds the centre of the screen while its photograph passes behind it, and is then pushed out by the next panel's verb. Use mix-blend-mode: difference in white, or one solid colour tested on every image. One sentence at 18px sits in the bottom-left corner of each panel over a neutral scrim limited to that corner. There is no separate heading: the verbs, read in order, are both the heading and the sequence.
sections.mobile: Panels stay 100svh, each photograph cropped to a vertical slice. The verb is 24vw, still sticky at the centre. The sentence sits along the bottom over a scrim at 16px, full width with 16px margins.

sections.name: Address in display rows
sections.blueprint: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number. Each row is about 150px tall with the text sitting in its lower third; rows are told apart by alternating two flat tones of the section colour as full-width bands, or by 28px of space alone. A sixth row holds a one-word greeting at the same size followed, 24px to its right and centred on the x-height, by a solid round button 0.9em across with an arrow, which opens the email or booking link. Street and phone rows are links (map, call). No heading and no form. Optionally, one small round photograph sits at the right end of the first row.
sections.mobile: Rows at 9.6vw with 16px insets, about 84px tall; the hours break onto two rows (days, then times). The greeting row becomes a full-width band in the accent colour with the round arrow button at its right end, 56px across.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: Kereliott
references.idea: A quiet house gets a quiet page: one dark field, one typeface, the name set as wide as the screen and photographs left to drift in generous darkness.
references.hero: Very dark green-black field with cream type. A two-line introductory sentence at about 30px sits top-left inside 30px margins; a small cream rectangular button sits top-right. The upper half is otherwise empty. The house name fills the full content width in a flared humanist sans, mixed case, with capitals about 19vw tall, its baseline at roughly 87% of the viewport height. Immediately beneath, separated by a gap of a few pixels, the top sliver of a full-width landscape photograph enters from the bottom edge.
references.type: A single face, Trust, in regular weight: a humanist sans with flared terminals and old-style figures. The wordmark is an oversized graphic; all other text is one size of about 20-30px plus tiny 10px photo captions. Hierarchy is position, not weight.
references.colour: #161c1a #eae8dc #222926 #1f2926 — Cream on green-black from top to bottom with no accent colour. The map is drawn in a tone barely lighter than the ground, so photographs supply all the colour.
references.imagery: Natural-light photos of a stone cottage, garden and deck with square corners, in mixed portrait and landscape crops at differing sizes. One full-width opener, then small images placed singly with tiny captions under the left corner.
references.layout: 30px margins, text held to the left 60% in one size. Photographs are staggered left and right at different widths with large dark gaps between, like pictures passed on a wall. The name and a booking button stay fixed in the top corners.

sections.description: A full-width landscape photograph runs margin to margin directly under the wordmark, followed after a gap by a four-line paragraph in the single text size, left-aligned and spanning about 85% of the width. There is no heading or label; the text simply continues the sentence begun at the top of the page.

After a left-aligned paragraph, a silhouette map of the region sits centre-left, about half the viewport wide, filled in a green only a few percent lighter than the background. Five towns are marked with small ring dots and tiny labels; only the house's town has a solid cream dot. No border, legend or frame.

Photographs are placed one or two per screen in a stagger: a portrait image about 30% wide against the left margin, a larger near-square one starting lower against the right margin, later a landscape image top-right of centre and a smaller one bottom-left. Each has a 10px caption under its left corner. More than half of every screen is empty dark ground.

Two short left-aligned sentences in the standard text size with underlined inline links to booking platforms and an email address, then a small cream certification badge. The footer is a single line at the very bottom: social link left, copyright centre, three underlined utility links right, with a tall empty gap above.

steal: Size the wordmark to fill the content width exactly and let the first photograph tuck directly under its baseline.
Draw a location map as a tone-on-tone silhouette with one filled dot among ring dots.
Use a single typeface in one weight and essentially one text size, creating hierarchy through placement and emptiness.

references.name: House of Honey
references.idea: A block-heavy wordmark pierced by a hairline script: the bold-against-delicate contrast is repeated at every scale, with giant pink script behind quiet serif statements.
references.hero: Top 42% is a flat blush-pink band; the bottom 58% is a full-bleed photograph of a bright living room, arched window on the centre axis, butting against the band with no margin. A tiny nav row sits at the very top with 8px side margins: block logo glyph and five links left, contact link with a small square arrow box far right. The wordmark fills the width edge to edge: two words in ultra-black extended caps, about 120px cap height, dark aubergine, with a hairline script 'of' 230px tall between them, overshooting above and below. Directly beneath, two two-line serif uppercase taglines at 31px, one flush left, one flush right.
references.type: Wordmark in ultra-black extended caps; statements in noeText serif, uppercase, 31–40px, tight tracking; nav and captions in neueHaasGrotesk around 14px; 'canora' hairline script for the connecting word and for cropped background words at 37vw. Three contrasting voices, each with one job.
references.colour: #edccbe #331917 #0e0e0e #f26fcb #ffffff — Blush pink and dark aubergine-brown alternate as full fields and as each other's text colour. Hot pink appears only in the oversized script and a 2px divider. Photographs bring saturated colour.
references.imagery: Editorial interior photography, saturated and daylight-lit. Hero is a full-bleed landscape crop; projects are portrait crops about 5:6 in a three-column grid with 4px gutters and square corners.
references.layout: Edge-to-edge with 8px outer margins. Typographic sections (small centred label, serif statement, cropped giant script) alternate with a three-column image grid. Blush and brown fields swap each section; hairline link rows close blocks. The footer is a full-width logo glyph.

sections.description: Dark aubergine field under the hero photo, separated by a 2px hot-pink line. A small sans label centred, then a three-line centred serif uppercase statement at about 31px in blush, 45% of the width. Behind it a hot-pink script phrase set near 37vw runs off both sides and is cut by the section's bottom edge, its ascenders rising into the statement. A smaller serif line follows.

Title card before the project grid. Blush field, nearly empty screen. A small label and a one-line serif uppercase heading about 40px sit centred at 55% height. The giant pink script returns, cropped by the bottom edge so only its top half shows and running off both sides.

Three columns edge to edge with 4px gutters and 8px outer margins. Portrait photos about 500×580px, square corners. Under each: an uppercase sans title at 14px and a grey line of GPS coordinates. Two rows, then a full-width hairline row with a text link left and a small square arrow box at the far right.

Brown field. The logo glyph is enlarged to full width and about a third of the screen: blush rectangles and quarter-circle arcs with 4px gaps, forming an abstract monogram. Below: four columns of small links, a hairline, two addresses in the first two columns, another hairline, then copyright left and a small blush button right.

steal: Set a wordmark edge to edge in ultra-heavy extended caps and thread a hairline script connecting word through it that overshoots the cap height both ways.
Use an oversized script word in one hot accent colour as a cropped background layer behind small, calm serif statements.
Split a tagline into two halves, flush left and flush right on the same baseline under the wordmark, instead of centring it.

references.name: Serotoninn
references.idea: A torn-paper seam splits the page in two, colour on white against greyscale on grey paper, to stage the brand's glam-versus-grunge line, with ultra-condensed heavy type straddling the tear.
references.hero: The viewport is split by a vertical torn-paper edge at 50%: left half pure white, right half a grey paper texture. A cut-out model stands dead centre, about 28% wide, running from 15% down off the bottom edge; her left half is full colour, her right half greyscale, the tear passing through her. Type is ultra-condensed heavy uppercase: the brand name at about 5.5vw top-left beneath a three-line mono menu; a two-line tagline right-aligned at mid-height on the right; and at bottom centre a two-word line at 8.2vw, first word red and second white, overlapping the dress, with a bracketed link beneath. Small centred logo at top, three mono links top-right.
references.type: Thunder extra-bold in uppercase, set tight, for all display lines (118px in the hero, similar for category words, sometimes rotated 90 degrees). PP Fraktion Mono uppercase at about 11px for nav, labels and prices; Inter for small body. Square brackets and parentheses wrap secondary words and counts.
references.colour: #fdfdfd #d8d8d8 #0a0a0a #e8352b #fff9f7 #2a2fb0 — White, paper grey and black with red as the single interface accent (one headline word, section labels). Garment colour (cobalt, yellow, satin tan) supplies the rest. One full black campaign band.
references.imagery: Studio fashion photography of models, cut out or on white seamless, in tall portrait crops. The hero splits one image into colour and greyscale along a torn-paper edge, and the torn edge returns as a divider over the footer video.
references.layout: About 2.5% margins. Sections carry red numbered mono labels at top-left. The layout changes every time: a label column with a product trio; a full-bleed black video; a horizontal row of tall category cards; a two-up split with a torn seam; a footer laid over video.

sections.description: New arrivals. The left 25% is a nearly empty column holding only a red numbered mono label at top, a bracketed link, and two tiny parenthesised notes further down. The right 60% holds three product images side by side with 4px gaps, each about 3:4, the middle one a tight crop of the same garment. Two carry a black brush-stroke tag with white condensed text in the top-left corner. Name and price sit under each in mono.

Categories as a horizontally scrolling row of five tall white cards, about 2:3 with 8px gaps, each showing a full-length cut-out model. The category name is set in the heavy condensed face rotated 90 degrees, running up the card's left edge from the bottom; a bracketed item count sits bottom-right in mono. The fifth card is cropped by the viewport edge.

Two-up split filling the viewport: two half-width photos of models on pale grounds, divided by a vertical torn-paper edge instead of a straight line. Each half has a category word in heavy condensed type at about 3.5vw bottom-left with a smaller parenthesised word attached like a suffix, and a bracketed count bottom-right.

A dark campaign video is cut off by a horizontal torn-paper edge, below which a taupe-grey ground holds the footer. Mono link clusters sit top-left and top-right. A cut-out model stands about 40% across, overlapping a very large condensed wordmark in darker grey so that letters pass behind her. Bottom-left, a subscribe line in white condensed type with a bracketed suffix; an underlined email field at right.

steal: Split one photograph along a torn-paper edge into a colour half and a greyscale half on different grounds, and let a two-word headline change colour across the same seam.
Run category names in heavy condensed type rotated 90 degrees up the edge of tall product cards, with a bracketed item count in mono at the opposite corner.
Reuse a torn-paper edge as the divider between sections and over the footer instead of straight lines.
